channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: When Evaluation Dashboards Hide Silent Model Failures
item.description: A clean accuracy chart on a managed ML dashboard can hide leakage, drift, and slice-level failures that only careful, manual evaluation will reveal.

item.title: Reading an MLOps Certification Syllabus: Gaps and Gains
item.description: MLOps syllabuses teach you the pipeline plumbing well, but often skip the harder judgement calls around evaluation, drift, and leakage.

item.title: Bootcamps vs Self-Taught Paths: What Portfolios Reveal
item.description: Bootcamp or self-taught, the credential says little. The portfolio, read carefully, says almost everything about how someone actually thinks.

item.title: How to Read an Evaluation Section Like a Reviewer
item.description: Skip the leaderboard instinct. Learn to interrogate splits, baselines, and variance the way a careful reviewer does, not the way a skimmer does.

item.title: Knowledge Distillation: Shrinking a Model Without Breaking It
item.description: Distillation can quietly shrink a model's failure modes into a smaller package. Here's how to check whether you've actually preserved behaviour, not just accuracy.

item.title: Multi-Task Learning: When a Shared Backbone Helps or Hurts
item.description: A shared backbone sounds efficient, but it only pays off when tasks actually agree on what a good representation looks like.

item.title: Warm Restarts and Why a Constant Learning Rate Rarely Wins
item.description: A constant learning rate forces a single compromise between speed and stability. Schedules, especially warm restarts, let you have both at different points in training.

item.title: Weight Decay Versus Dropout: Different Jobs Entirely
item.description: Weight decay shrinks parameters towards zero; dropout forces redundancy across units. Treating them as interchangeable is a common and costly mistake.

item.title: Regression Versus Classification: Framing Messy Problems
item.description: The real modelling decision often happens before training starts: is this a number to predict or a category to assign? Choose badly and you fight the problem forever.

item.title: Data-Centric NLP: Clean Your Corpus Before the Model
item.description: A messy corpus quietly caps your model's ceiling. Here is a practical, leakage-aware approach to cleaning text data before you touch a single hyperparameter.

item.title: Vision Transformers Explained from the Patch Embedding Upward
item.description: How a grid of pixels becomes a sequence a transformer can read, and why that single design choice explains almost everything else about ViTs.

item.title: Explaining a Transformer's Attention Mechanism Simply
item.description: How I explain transformer attention to non-technical interviewers using a room full of conversations, not maths.

item.title: What NLP Techniques Survive Contact With Small Data
item.description: Most NLP advice assumes thousands of labelled examples. Here is what genuinely works when you have a few hundred, and how to prove it honestly.

item.title: LLM Arenas: Pairwise Preference Is Not Accuracy
item.description: Arena win rates measure relative preference, not correctness. Confusing the two can make a fluent, wrong model look like the best model.

item.title: Degree, Course, or Portfolio: What Really Teaches Fine-Tuning
item.description: Degrees, courses, and portfolios each promise fine-tuning skills. Only one forces you to fail, debug, and rerun until the numbers hold up.

item.title: LLM Benchmarks Decoded: What a Leaderboard Score Tests
item.description: A leaderboard score measures performance on one fixed test set under one prompting scheme. It is not a certificate of general intelligence.

item.title: Fine-Tuning: One Word, Several Very Different Ideas
item.description: Fine-tuning sounds like a small tweak everywhere it's used, but in ML it can mean anything from adjusting a few layers to retraining a whole model. The distinction matters.

item.title: Quantifying Uncertainty: The Confidence Intervals You Skip
item.description: A model's reported accuracy is a guess with error bars nobody drew. Here is how to draw them and why it changes conclusions.

item.title: Picking a First Computer Vision Job: Lab vs Startup vs Team
item.description: Research lab, startup, or industry team: the right first CV job depends on what skill you want to compound, not on prestige.

item.title: Data Science Job Adverts Decoded: What Years Signals
item.description: Job adverts treat years of experience as a precise filter, but it is a noisy proxy for skill. Here is how to read it properly.
